rule.description: The Dylint rule SCATTERED_SIGNAL_STOP_POLICY reports every call site that re-states a signal-stop-policy decision as a local match table: class=stop_signal_resolution for two-tuple matches over (Option<Signal>, Option<Signal>) resolving which signal a stop uses, and class=stop_request_classification for single-Signal matches with one arm naming the Interrupt | Terminate stop-request pair. A class is a shotgun-surgery violation once two or more distinct functions re-state it, because any change to that policy then requires one coordinated edit per host function; a lone table is the policy's single rightful home and passes.

checks.description: Sites that resolve which signal a stop of the watched command uses by re-stating the (signal, stop-signal) option pair as a local two-tuple match table, instead of asking one shared owner.
checks.detected_relation: call function -> local (Option<Signal>, Option<Signal>) stop-resolution table
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The decision of which signal stops the command belongs to one owner; each extra host function means a change to that resolution policy (defaults, precedence, option interaction) must be replayed in every one of them -- the small-edits-everywhere shotgun pattern.

matches.evidence: Ctrl-C quit path (config.rs:409): action.quit_gracefully is fed by an inline match over (signal, stop_signal) choosing the stop signal or the built-in Terminate fallback.
Once-mode timeout (config.rs:456): the timeout stop hoists the same (signal, stop_signal) resolution table into a local before job.stop_with_signal.
Interactive stop key (config.rs:528): job.stop_with_signal receives the resolution table inline.
Interactive restart key (config.rs:547): job.restart_with_signal receives the same resolution table inline.
--on-busy-update restart while running (config.rs:701): job.restart_with_signal re-states the same option-pair table.
The pre-existing lone resolver (config.rs:805): the busy-signalling variant of the same option-pair table, where --signal legitimately wins; already a policy home before the other sites appeared.
Spawned timeout watcher for --timeout (config.rs:1493): a further copy of the resolution table deciding the timeout's stop signal.

checks.description: Sites that classify which signals count as a stop request (the Interrupt | Terminate pair) by re-stating the pair inside a local match table, instead of asking one shared owner such as a predicate on the Signal type.
checks.detected_relation: signal consumer -> local Interrupt|Terminate stop-request classification table
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: Which signals mean "stop now" is one policy fact about Signal; each extra host function is another place a maintainer must remember to edit when that set changes -- the shotgun-surgery relation.

matches.evidence: Emit-only mode quit (config.rs:198): the action handler scans received signals and sets a quit flag when its local match table classifies a signal as the Interrupt/Terminate stop-request pair.

Unmapped-signal quit check (config.rs:588): the main action handler classifies the same pair again, with an arm guarded by the signal-map lookup, re-stating the policy with a local variation of its shape.

Signal event source (signal.rs:157): the runtime-side copy of the classification, hoisted into a priority decided by the same Interrupt|Terminate arm; the cross-crate spread that makes the pair's definition impossible to change from one place.

excluded.structure: crates/supervisor/src/job/ -- stop/stop_with_signal and signal/signal_with_signal platform dispatch (cfg!(unix)/cfg!(windows) branches)
excluded.reason: Platform dispatch choosing how a signal is delivered, not a re-statement of the stop policy; the rule requires the decision table itself, not a call into it.

excluded.structure: signal == Signal::TerminalSuspend / sig == Signal::Interrupt style equality comparisons
excluded.reason: Plain boolean comparisons are not the pair-classification or option-resolution table shape the rule defines.

excluded.structure: crates/signals/src/lib.rs -- Display/inverse-signal-name mapping and Serde conversions
excluded.reason: Presentation and serialization mappings enumerate all variants; they do not decide a stop policy.

excluded.structure: while let / if let / await desugared matches, and macro-generated tables whose match node is attributed to the macro definition
excluded.reason: Not source-written stop-policy decision tables at an analyzable span; the rule reports deliberate match tables only.

excluded.structure: Keyboard EOF and interactive key handling in crates/cli/src/config.rs
excluded.reason: Keyboard lifecycle concerns unrelated to the signal stop policy.
